headline: Predicting spatial gene expression from H&E histology via transcriptomic foundation priors
label: Histology Spatial Transcriptomics Integration
summary: Routine H&E histology is now paired with transcriptomic foundation-model priors and formal inference for imputed spatial transcriptomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inference of spatial gene expression from tissue measurements. Morpho-FM predicts spatial expression from routine H&E slides using a pretrained single-cell transcriptomic foundation-model prior. TIDEST addresses the downstream problem created by such reconstruction, providing differential expression inference on computationally reconstructed spatial transcriptomes with calibrated imputed values. Region-aware bridge modeling summarizes Visium colorectal and breast cancer sections into eight-region mesoscale representations, and surprisal analysis is applied to spatial transcriptomics of human glioblastoma. The remaining items, covering Perturb-seq response curves, multi-omics integration, receptor-to-transcription factor reconstruction, TCM immune recovery and proteomic tissue inference, share omics integration but not the spatial-histology focus. What is new is statistical validity after imputation alongside histology-to-expression transfer.
